noradrenalene inhibits the inhibitory feedback from the mitral cell dendrites to the soma, and glutamate and asparate augment the inhibitory dendritic feedback.
noradrenalines inhibits the feedback onto olfactory bulb relay neurones and that glutamate and asparatate enhances the inhibitory feedback.
noradrenaline enhances excitatory responses in the olfactory relay neurones of the olfactory bulb through disinhibition of the feedback inhibitory circuit.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the cellular mechanisms underlying the enhancement of sensory transmission by noradrenaline.
the role of noradrenalines in sensory processing.
the modulation of synaptic inhibition in the ol-factory bulb by noradrenaline, glutamate and aspaate.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the noradrenaline system in the olfactory system has an excitatory effect on the output of the system.

noradrenalinergic modulation of dendrodentritic inhibition in the rat olfactory bulb is due to a direct action of noradrenalin on the dendrites of the granule cell, and that the action of the inhibitory transmitter is mediated by N-methyl-D-aspartate receptors.
noradrenalene is a powerful inhibitor of the inhibitory interneuron and thus facilitates excitatory transmission.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
noradrenalene and glutamate are excitatory to relay neurones while aspartate and GABA are inhibitory.
noradreinegic modulation of the olfactory bulb is consistent with a disinhibitory role.
noradrenalinerelays neurones in the olfactory system, and that noradrenalinesensitizes relay neurones to glutamate/aspartate, while glutamate/aspartatesensitizes relayneurones to noradrenaline.
The main takeaway from our work is that
noradrener-gic modulation of dendritic inhibition is likely to be important in a variety of brain regions.
noradrenalines actions are not limited to the facilitation of sensory input.
noradrener-gic transmission in the CNS may be more complicated than previously thought.
